resumen: With one knee and one hand on a bench, you row a kettlebell towards your hip with the elbow close to the body. Like the dumbbell row, with the weight hanging below the hand.
ejecucion: Rest the knee and hand of the same side on the bench, back straight and almost parallel to the floor, and the other foot on the floor.
Pick up the kettlebell with your free hand, palm facing your body, and let it hang with a straight arm.
Row by driving your elbow back, close to your body, until the kettlebell reaches hip height.
Lower under control until your arm is straight; when the set is done, switch sides.
If your torso rotates to lift it, lower the weight.
matices: We have found no study measuring the kettlebell row itself. It is the same movement as the one-arm dumbbell row, the main difference being that the weight hangs below the handle instead of sitting on either side of the hand.
